main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing a medical alert bracelet (visible or covered) despite the new no-accessories uniform rule before tomorrow's area manager visit

A-B.evidence: B says the memo has no medical exception (5) and A agrees 'She's right' (6); but B then asks why she wasn't told she could cover earrings (8) and A says rule applies to everyone (9).

A-C.evidence: C: 'The memo is from head office. We can't make exceptions. Agent A is right' (11); C backs A again on the sweatband (26).

A-D.evidence: A insists it must come off and won't allow covering or explaining to manager (3, 13, 18, 23, 31); D keeps pressing 'either my health or my job?' (32).

B-C.evidence: Both rely on the memo having no exceptions (5, 11), but they never address each other directly.

B-D.evidence: B says the memo has no medical exception (5), but also asks if covering is okay (8), partly taking up D's cover idea.

C-D.evidence: C rejects D's sweatband idea: 'A sweatband is an accessory too. That doesn't fix it' (26), and says no exceptions can be made (11).
